title: Microsoft Word: choose the model used by Copilot Agent Mode on the web
summary: Hold: restricting Anthropic to a pilot group does not establish that only that group can see every third-party model. The roadmap facts match, but the briefing also assumes an undocumented change from automatic provider routing to user choice.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; front matter: changes
claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page specifically describes model selection in Agent Mode in Word.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Agent Mode Word choose model picker license admin default; Word Agent Mode model selection admin disable switch per model default license Copilot Credits. Opened Learn wordexcelppt-agents, copilot-overview and release-notes; these describe other agents or broader Word model selection.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot generally lets users select different models using the UI model selector.
claims.quote: You can select different models by using the model selector in the UI.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot generally uses a real-time router by default to adjust the model based on the prompt.
claims.quote: By default, Copilot uses a real-time router to adjust the underlying model it uses based on your prompt.

claims.claim: Whether Word Agent Mode follows the overview's real-time routing pattern is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Agent Mode Word choose model picker license admin default; Word Agent Mode default. Opened copilot-overview, wordexcelppt-agents, release-notes and Support Get started editing with Copilot in Office; none states this routing pattern for Word Agent Mode.

claims.claim: The 11 August 2026 release notes contain the Web Word entry 'Choose Anthropic models when editing with Copilot in Word'.
claims.quote:
August 11, 2026
Updates released between July 28, 2026, and August 11, 2026.
Choose Anthropic models when editing with Copilot in Word [Web]

claims.claim: That release-notes entry says Word editing supports Anthropic models alongside OpenAI models.
claims.quote: You can choose to select Anthropic models, in addition to OpenAI models, when editing a Word document using Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly identify the August Word release-notes entry as roadmap item 545012.
claims.quote: Searched: Word Edit with Copilot model select; Word Agent Mode model picker admin policy. Read the August 11 release-notes Word entry: it links roadmap ID 558440, not 545012. The supplied roadmap record has no moreInfoLink identifying the two capabilities.

claims.claim: This change moves selection of the AI provider handling a document prompt from Microsoft's routing to the individual user.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Agent Mode Word choose model picker license admin default; Word Agent Mode default. Read copilot-overview, release-notes and Support Get started editing with Copilot in Office. No passage establishes prior provider routing or that this item's model choice changes provider.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of Why it matters with: 'The roadmap plans to give users a choice of model for their Word task.'

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft 365 admin center path reaches the Anthropic control used to assign provider access.
claims.quote:
select Copilot > Settings > View all.
Select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors.
under Available subprocessors for your organization, select Anthropic
Under Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences, select your users or groups
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and its rendered path to 'Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization > Anthropic > Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences > users or groups', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/connect-to-ai-subprocessor.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for assigning access through this Anthropic provider setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph beta AI provider subprocessor Anthropic access setting API PowerShell; Anthropic Graph provider settings API. Read connect-to-ai-subprocessor and copilot-ai-provider-user-sec-group-access; results identify UI controls, not a Graph or PowerShell operation setting provider access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Claude models in Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently outside EU Data Boundary and applicable in-country processing commitments.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and when applicable, in-country processing commitments.

claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention are off by default in all scenarios and require separate tenant-admin opt-in.
claims.quote: Anthropic models with Data Retention ... are off by default for all scenarios ... No users will have access to these models until the tenant admin explicitly opts in to enable use of Anthropic models with Data Retention.

claims.claim: The Anthropic overview says Claude models are disabled by default in the EU, EFTA and UK.
claims.quote: Customers within the EU Data Boundary and customers in the UK have Claude models disabled by default.
claims.fix: After this regional-default statement, add: 'The separate apps-only guidance says the setting is enabled by default for EU, EFTA and UK tenants created after 25 March 2026; check the actual tenant setting.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/copilot-anthropic-apps, which states 'This setting is enabled by default for tenants in the EU, EFTA, and UK that were created after March 25, 2026.'

claims.claim: Microsoft enables Claude models by default for most commercial-cloud customers outside the EU, EFTA and UK.
claims.quote: Microsoft enables Claude models on by default for most customers in commercial cloud (excluding EU/EFTA and UK).
